subject.title: Configurable per-workflow base/target branch (workspace cut from and PR opened against something other than the repo default branch)
subject.body:
**Spec:** §5.2.4/§6.2 (workspace base derivation), §5.6 (canonical publish snippet) · **Depends on:** —

## Problem

BEN's workspace provider has no concept of a base branch other than the repository's actual
GitHub default branch. `internal/workspace/workspace.go`'s `remoteDefaultBranch` reads the
remote HEAD symref, and a fresh issue's workspace branch is always cut from that fetched head
(`workspace.go:761,843,868`). The canonical publish snippet (SPEC §5.6) also hardcodes "open a
pull request against the default branch."

This surfaced on a real deployment: `NFTYDoor/nftydoor-admin` mirrors a Bitbucket repository —
GitHub `main` must stay a clean, GitHub-authored-commit-free mirror, and a whole stabilization
epic requires every BEN-authored branch to be cut from, and every PR opened against, a
dedicated `switchboard-stabilization` branch instead. Changing the repo's actual GitHub default
branch is explicitly a non-goal of that epic (it would violate the mirror invariant a different
way). There is no other way today to make BEN base and publish against a non-default branch —
not a config key, not a documented workaround, and it isn't named in §13's deferred extensions
either.

## Proposal (for discussion, not a locked design)

Add an optional `workspace.base_branch` (or similar) config key: when set, `Prepare` fetches and
bases fresh workspaces on that ref instead of the repository's default branch, and the canonical
publish snippet's PR-target instruction uses it instead of "the default branch." Needs a decision
on:

- whether the base ref is validated to exist at `Ready`-time (readiness failure) or load time;
- interaction with the remote-first reattach logic (§6.2) — reattaching to an existing
  `ben/<workspace_key>` branch should presumably still take precedence over the configured base
  for a fresh prepare;
- whether this belongs in `workspace` or is closer to a `publish`-block concern, since it affects
  both the git base and the PR target.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A workflow can configure a non-default base/target branch and have BEN's workspace
      provider and canonical publish snippet both honor it.
- [ ] `ben config effective` surfaces the configured value (or its default-branch fallback)
      with provenance, per §5.8.
- [ ] Structural validation rejects an obviously malformed ref name at load; existence is a
      readiness concern, not a load concern (mirrors how `publish.value` is handled, §5.5).
- [ ] `make check` green (evidence in the PR)
